_note: The breakdown sentence is split into a prefix and a suffix around the computed figure rather than being one string with a placeholder, because no tool template in the fleet does mid-string interpolation and introducing it would be a shared-vocabulary change (owner ruling 2026-07-29). The cost is that a translator cannot reorder the sentence. Recorded as a real limitation, not hidden.

balance_label.llm_guidance: Label for the balance input. Say OUTSTANDING: the figure wanted is what is left to pay, not the amount originally borrowed, and people supply the wrong one if the label is vague.

balance_default.llm_guidance: Starting balance. Part of the equivalence fingerprint -- the acceptance criteria scale it and assert the resulting settlement figures, so changing it re-baselines this tool's golden values.

apr_default.llm_guidance: Starting APR. Part of the equivalence fingerprint (see balance_default).

result_heading.llm_guidance: Heading over the figure. Keep ESTIMATED. This is an indicative calculation from two inputs; the binding figure is the settlement quote the lender issues, and a heading that omits the hedge reads as though this tool produces one.

settlement_days.llm_guidance: Days of additional interest a lender may add. 58 is the UK convention -- a 28-day notice period plus 30 days, under the Consumer Credit (Early Settlement) Regulations 2004. It is a DEFAULT, not a universal rule: individual agreements differ, which is why the surrounding copy says 'usually'. A non-UK site must set this to whatever its own regime allows, and if there is no such regime the tool does not apply at all.

days_in_year.llm_guidance: Divisor turning the annual rate into a daily one. 365 matches the original. Some lenders use 360 for daily accrual; changing it moves every figure this tool prints, so change it only against a lender's stated basis, never for tidiness.

breakdown_prefix.llm_guidance: Text before the interest charge in the breakdown line. The trailing space is significant -- the currency symbol follows immediately. Keep 'approx.': the figure is an estimate and the sentence is the only place that is said near the number.

breakdown_suffix.llm_guidance: Text after the interest charge. The leading space is significant. If you change settlement_days, change this too -- they are two fields stating the same number and nothing enforces that they agree.

currency_symbol.llm_guidance: Prefixed to both figures as a literal, not derived from the locale.

locale.llm_guidance: BCP-47 locale used for thousands separators and decimal marks on the settlement figure ONLY. The breakdown line uses toFixed and ignores it, so the two lines can disagree about grouping on a five-figure balance -- a known cosmetic inconsistency, preserved deliberately from the original because fixing it moves the golden values.
